Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testMath369` invokes `BisectionSolver.solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)` at line 101 expecting to solve the function within bounds. However, the implementation of this method simply calls `solve(min, max)` without passing the function `f`. The method `solve(double min, double max)` is marked as deprecated but internally calls `solve(f, min, max)`. The problem is that the function field `f` inherited from `UnivariateRealSolverImpl` is never initialized/set by `solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)`. Consequently, when the deprecated `solve(double min, double max)` calls `solve(f, min, max)`, `f` is null, leading to a `NullPointerException`.

The correct approach would be for `solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)` to delegate to `solve(f, min, max)` (which sets `f` properly) instead of calling the deprecated `solve(min, max)`. The current bug report explicitly outlines this issue and mentions that the member variable `f` is null, causing the exception.

Hence, the root cause is the inappropriate delegation inside `BisectionSolver.solve(UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial)` to `solve(min, max)` without initializing `f`.

No other recent bug reports appear relevant to this specific problem.

Next step: Suggest a fix in the `BisectionSolver` class focusing on the `solve` method variants that handle the function parameter.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
